title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes of conversations with Deligne on 30.5 and 5.6, almost certainly 1981. They sit at the start of the 'Teichmüllerie' dossier; the next page discusses the stable compactification of the modular stacks M_{g,ν}. The four items all serve one programme: understanding the Teichmüller and modular 'tower' both topologically and arithmetically. That means finite subgroups of mapping class groups, their fixed points on Teichmüller space (a cell), and the structure of the profinite surface group as an arithmetic object.

(1) Finite groups acting topologically on surfaces. Grothendieck proposes Smith theory, in its spectral-sequence (Borel-seminar) form. For a p-group acting on a mod-p homology manifold, the fixed-point set is again a mod-p (Čech) cohomology manifold. One reduces to elements of prime order. On a surface the fixed set is then locally a homology manifold of dimension ≤ 1. Hence it is locally connected (dimension 1 is the case that matters, e.g. orientation-reversing involutions), so arc-connected, and in low dimension (Wilder) it is a genuine manifold: isolated points or a 1-manifold. This is one step towards showing that topological finite actions on surfaces are conjugate to conformal or anticonformal ones (Kerékjártó–Brouwer–Eilenberg). That in turn identifies finite subgroups of the (extended) mapping class group with automorphism groups of (real) Riemann surfaces.

(2) A warning example from Bing (1952). There is an involution of S^3 whose fixed set is the Alexander horned sphere. From it one gets an involution of B^3 with a wild fixed 2-disc, whose restriction to S^2 = ∂B^3 is the perfectly standard complex conjugation (reflection in the equator). So a standard boundary action does not force the action on the ball to be the cone of the boundary action, even in dimension 3 (topologically).

(3) A conjecture attributed to Deligne, about which Grothendieck notes he did not understand the mechanism. There should exist simplicial (PL) actions of finite groups on B^n (n ≥ 5?) that are not cones of actions on S^{n-1}. This is linked to the fact that a finite group action on a sphere with a fixed point need not lie in a topological conjugate of O(n). Modern mechanism: fixed sets in PL actions on balls can be contractible non-ball manifolds (Mazur-type) with homology-sphere boundaries. Via the double suspension theorem, non-locally-linear actions on spheres exist. More generally there is the Floyd–Richardson / Oliver theory of fixed sets of actions on discs. Implicit relevance: the Teichmüller space T_{g,ν} is a cell, and its Thurston compactification is a closed ball with boundary sphere PMF. The mapping class group acts on it, so whether finite group actions on such balls are 'conical/linear' bears on Nielsen realization and on the local orbifold structure of M_{g,ν}.

(4) Arithmetic item. To describe the 'symplectic' structure on the (profinite) fundamental group of a smooth proper connected curve over an algebraically closed field, one must use the intersection form. It takes values in \hat T = \hat Z(1), the Tate twist. In modern terms: the profinite surface group is a Poincaré-duality pro-group of dimension 2 with dualizing module \hat Z(1). The cup product H^1 × H^1 → H^2 = \hat Z(1) gives the Weil-pairing symplectic form on the abelianization. Grothendieck wants a non-abelian refinement: a cohomological, hence étale and Galois-equivariant, definition of intersections of 'paths' in the sense of covering theory. The drawings show oriented paths between base points that cross, and loops based at points. This is exactly the homotopy intersection form / intersection of paths (Turaev 1978; Papakyriakopoulos) and the Goldman bracket (1986). Last line: 'give a cohomological theory of a curve in the pro-[?]…', i.e. a cohomological description of the curve inside the pro-finite (groupoid/diagram) setting.
errors: Item 2: 'une boule de pts fixes' cannot be right. A nontrivial periodic homeomorphism of a connected manifold cannot fix an open set (Newman's theorem), so the fixed set must be a wild 2-disc (half of the Alexander horned sphere) whose boundary is the equator fixed by complex conjugation. Most likely a transcription misreading of 'disque'.

Item 1: Smith theory applies to p-groups (elements of prime order). For general finite groups one must reduce to cyclic subgroups of prime order, and the conclusion is a Čech cohomology manifold mod p. Passing from 'locally connected' to an actual 1-manifold needs Wilder's low-dimensional results. These are gaps only in the sketch, not errors.
Item 3 is explicitly conjectural ('il doit y avoir', 'n ≥ 5 ??', 'J'ai pas bien compris comment'); no construction is given.

ideas.what: Use Smith theory (spectral sequences) to show fixed sets of finite groups acting on surfaces are homology manifolds, hence locally/arc connected
ideas.modern_name: Smith theory; Kerékjártó–Eilenberg theorem that periodic surface homeomorphisms are conjugate to isometries
ideas.usually_credited_to: P.A. Smith (1938), Borel seminar (1960); Kerékjártó, Brouwer, Eilenberg (1919–1934)

ideas.what: Bing's involution with wild fixed set (Alexander horned sphere); ball version with standard complex conjugation on the boundary, so ball action ≠ cone of boundary action
Finite (PL) group actions on discs not conical over the boundary sphere; finite actions on spheres with fixed points not topologically conjugate to orthogonal actions
ideas.modern_name: Non-locally-linear / exotic actions on discs and spheres (Floyd–Richardson, Oliver fixed-set theory, double suspension examples)

ideas.what: Symplectic structure on the profinite fundamental group of a proper curve via intersection form valued in \hat Z(1)
ideas.modern_name: Poincaré-duality pro-group of dimension 2, Weil pairing, Galois-equivariant symplectic form

ideas.what: Define cohomologically (étale-wise) the intersection of paths/loops in the sense of covering theory, i.e. a non-abelian intersection pairing on the profinite fundamental groupoid of a curve
ideas.modern_name: Turaev homotopy intersection form, Goldman bracket / Turaev cobracket, and their Hodge/ℓ-adic (motivic) versions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Turaev (1978), Goldman (1986), Massuyeau–Turaev (2013), Kawazumi–Kuno; Hodge-theoretic version Hain (c. 2020)

missed.claim: Already in 1981, Grothendieck (with Deligne) asks for a purely cohomological, hence arithmetic and Galois-equivariant, definition of intersections of paths on an algebraic curve. This is a profinite/étale Goldman–Turaev structure refining the \hat Z(1)-valued symplectic form. Later work makes it Hodge-theoretic and motivic (Hain), with ℓ-adic and Galois aspects in the Kawazumi–Kuno / Alekseev–Kawazumi–Kuno–Naef circle, but not attributed to this source.
missed.quote: Question de définir cohomologiquement les intersections de "chemins" (au sens théorie des revêtements)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the arithmetic Goldman–Turaev Lie bialgebra and its relation to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. It documents that the anabelian/Teichmüller programme envisaged a non-abelian intersection theory on profinite surface groups, a theme only systematically developed decades later.

missed.claim: Topological input is put alongside the arithmetic programme. Items 1–3 (Smith theory, non-conical finite actions on balls) are juxtaposed with Teichmüller theory. This suggests an intended route to fixed points of finite subgroups of the mapping class group on the Teichmüller cell or its Thurston ball compactification, together with a caution that such actions need not be conical or linear.
missed.quote: Il doit y avoir des actions simpliciales de groupes finis sur B^n (n ≥ 5 ??) qui ne sont pas le cône d'une action sur S^{n-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly historical, showing how Grothendieck approached Nielsen realization (Kerckhoff 1983) and orbifold structure via fixed-point topology. Mathematically it is subsumed by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: Most content consists of classical topology facts recorded from conversation. The one notable item is the early explicit call for a cohomological/arithmetic definition of intersections of paths on curves, prefiguring the Hodge/Galois-theoretic Goldman–Turaev theory. It is only a question with sketches, not a result.
transcription_corrections: Item 2: 'ayant une boule de pts fixes' should likely read 'ayant un disque de pts fixes' (wild disc, half of the Alexander horned sphere); 'sauvage' is an interlinear insertion.
Item 1: 'donc en dim 1 [?] loc. connexe' — the handwriting is ambiguous; the sense is 'hence (in dimension 1) locally connected, hence arc-connected'.
Item 4: 'sur le corps des [?]' probably reads 'sur le corps alg. clos' (over an algebraically closed field).
Item 4: 'à valeurs dans \hat T' — \hat T denotes \hat Z(1) (Tate module of roots of unity).
Item 3: the insertions 'simpliciales', 'une sphère avec pt fixe' and 'topologique' are interlinear corrections replacing struck-out text (struck: something like 'cycliques', 'une sphère').
